object_description: platformed building with a landscape-facing office ring and roof terrace
design_condition: The building follows the surrounding campus scale while using the slope to arrange central spaces on successive platforms and connect the lower entrance to the roof terrace.

positive.statement: Its volumetry and geometry continue the scale of the nearby buildings without imposing itself as a totem.
The project sensitively integrates the site's topographical constraints as design elements.
The programmatic order is clear and inventive.
The sloped interior circulation convincingly recreates a walk through natural terrain.
The office ring opens generously to the landscape and reveals the interior life of the building.
The structural system is flexible and scalable, with a regular framework and reasonable spans.
The facade and roof lighting provide controlled, consistent illumination to the offices and common spaces.
The proposed technical principles are consistent and achievable.

negative.statement: The central circulation organization does not convince the entire jury.
The mound installation is strongly questioned because it requires major ground reworking and may erase the original topography.
The proposed photovoltaic sunshade system is too complex and may create future technical problems.
The large glazed surfaces, especially the roof, raise doubts about overheating control.
The building's poor compactness weakens its construction-ecology performance.
The cost evaluation places the project well beyond the announced target.
The concept appeals to the jury but raises questions about its suitability for the intended program.
